title: Topological State-Aware Simulation Framework for Inter-Satellite Twin-Field QKD Networks
abstract: Inter-satellite links (ISLs) are the mandatory backbone for global quantum networks. While Twin-Field Quantum Key Distribution (TF-QKD) successfully surpasses linear rate-loss bounds, its extreme phase sensitivity makes it highly vulnerable to dynamic, non-IID (Independent and Identically Distributed) orbital environments. In composable finite-key analyses governed by the Generalized Entropy Accumulation Theorem (GEAT), traditional adaptive post-selection heuristics either violate strict independence conditions or incur massive second-order penalties that collapse the secret key rate. To overcome this, we introduce a reference-only topological post-selection oracle. By modeling the constellation as a Cellular Sheaf and applying Topological Data Analysis (TDA), our protocol derives a public acceptance event ($Ω$) exclusively from classical beacon telemetry. To rigorously validate this mechanism, we develop a modular simulation framework equipped with stochastic noise injection and an explicit GEAT security ledger. Simulations across 2,000-5,000 km ISL separations compare the same Hodge-Koopman gate with TDA disabled and enabled. At 2,000 km, the median conditional candidate rates are $2.14 \times 10^{-6}$ and $5.87 \times 10^{-7}$ bit per emitted pulse, respectively; both configurations return zero at 3,000-5,000 km. TDA is active in all 4,788 evaluated windows, but does not extend the positive-candidate range in this scenario. These exported rates are conditional numerical candidates: the full protocol-level composable-security proof remains incomplete and the certified composable rate is therefore zero throughout.
summary: This paper introduces a novel topological framework using Topological Data Analysis (TDA) to secure Quantum Key Distribution over dynamic inter-satellite links. By modeling the network state as a Cellular Sheaf and deriving acceptance criteria from classical beacon telemetry, it aims to overcome phase sensitivity issues caused by orbital noise. While showing promising candidate rates, the authors caution that the full composable security proof is not yet complete.
main_problem: The extreme phase sensitivity of Twin-Field QKD over dynamic Inter-Satellite Links (ISLs) makes traditional post-selection heuristics fail in non-IID orbital environments.
main_result: A reference-only topological post-selection oracle, utilizing Topological Data Analysis (TDA) on a Cellular Sheaf model, is proposed to derive public acceptance events from classical telemetry.
method: The protocol models the constellation as a Cellular Sheaf and applies TDA metrics (like persistent homology) to filter out noise sources that violate security assumptions in finite-key analysis.
model_or_system: The system is an ISL constellation undergoing dynamic orbital changes, modeled using physical components like pointing jitter (log-normal fades) and phase drift (Gauss–Markov process).

paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem (TF-QKD vulnerability), introduces the topological framework using Cellular Sheaves/TDA on public telemetry, simulates the protocol under noise, and compares TDA's effect against baseline methods while noting the incompleteness of the final security proof.
why_interesting: It directly addresses quantum networking challenges by integrating advanced mathematical tools (TDA) to handle complex, non-stationary environmental noise inherent in space-based quantum communication links.
